gloss: to get an idea; to find inspiration; to conceive of an idea

definitions.gloss: to get an idea; to find inspiration; to conceive of an idea
definitions.explanation: To arrive at a creative concept or idea, often by drawing on an external source of inspiration such as a real event, another work, or a personal experience. A somewhat literary expression used in artistic and intellectual contexts.

examples.japanese: {散歩|さんぽ}{中|ちゅう}に{着想|ちゃくそう}を{得|え}た。
examples.english: I got an idea during a walk.

examples.japanese: この{小説|しょうせつ}は{実話|じつわ}から{着想|ちゃくそう}を{得|え}たものだ。
examples.english: This novel was inspired by a true story.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{日本|にほん}の{伝統|でんとう}{工芸|こうげい}から{着想|ちゃくそう}を{得|え}て、{新|あたら}しいデザインを{生|う}み{出|だ}した。
examples.english: He drew inspiration from traditional Japanese crafts and created a new design.

notes:
A literary expression meaning to find or receive creative inspiration. {着想|ちゃくそう} means a concept or idea that comes to mind, and {得|え}る means to obtain. Often used in contexts of artistic creation, scientific discovery, or creative work. More formal and literary than simply ひらめく or アイデアを{思|おも}いつく.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ~から{着想|ちゃくそう}を{得|え}る: to draw inspiration from ~
- ~に{着想|ちゃくそう}を{得|え}た: inspired by ~ (modifying a noun)
- {着想|ちゃくそう}を{得|え}て: having gotten the idea, ...

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ヒントを{得|え}る — to get a hint/clue (less formal)
- インスピレーションを{受|う}ける — to receive inspiration (loanword, common in creative fields)
- {思|おも}いつく — to come up with (an idea) (more casual, everyday)
- ひらめく — to have a flash of inspiration (emphasizes sudden insight)
